title: Produce three competent examples of one foundational craft task
goal: Identify the core knowledge, tools, standards and safety limits of a small craft task and demonstrate repeatable acceptable work rather than one impressive attempt.
scope_note: Choose a safe non-regulated component. This does not authorize professional practice, hazardous equipment use or a claim of competence in an entire occupation.
burden: Twenty minutes to define the standard, three short attempts and a 15-minute comparison.
setup: Use the three complete fictional event briefs in the learning guide: Neighborhood Seed Swap, Repair Café Taster and Evening Sketch Walk. Use paper or a familiar text editor. Prepare one notice from each brief and check against the supplied F1–F5 accuracy and U1–U2 usability criteria. No event, contact route or address is real; keep the notices as practice artifacts. The guide supplies the facts, layout example, matching checks and a fresh contact-change retest.

actions.title: Identify the field’s basics and bound the sample task
actions.instructions: Read the guide’s event-notice preparation card, three briefs and F1–F5/U1–U2 standard. Identify the knowledge, tool and access method needed to turn supplied facts into a readable notice. Use this supplied product specification for the default. Separate mandatory factual accuracy and reading access from optional decoration. State that this samples a small communication-design component, not an entire profession, a legal notice or regulated work.
checks: Knowledge tools standard and safety limits are identified
Mandatory accuracy and access are separated from polish
The sample task is bounded within a broader craft
Unassessed professional capability is explicitly excluded

actions.title: Complete three independent attempts against the same standard
actions.instructions: Create a separate notice from each of the three supplied briefs. Keep comparable format, tools and support conditions, and verify which brief you are using before entering its facts. Preserve the original attempt before checking. Mark an incorrect, omitted or uninspected criterion explicitly instead of silently fixing the first result. You may use the blank layout pattern, but each notice must use its own facts. These fictional notices are not for real publication.
checks: Three distinct fact sets are attempted
The same standard and comparable conditions are used
Errors remain visible in the attempt record
No inaccurate notice is put into real use

actions.title: Have the work checked and target the unstable basic
actions.instructions: After preserving all three attempts, reveal each matching check or ask a freely willing intended reader to locate the five facts using the supplied standard. Label self-check, external review and untested access conditions separately. Inspect F1–F5 and U1–U2 for every output; attractive formatting cannot compensate for an incorrect date or missing contact. Identify an unstable basic, apply one specific correction and attempt the supplied contact-change retest. If no error was found, use the retest to check that a change is propagated accurately. Report only the component and conditions actually tested.
checks: All three outputs receive a consistent check
Self-review and external review are distinguished
A repeated weakness receives a concrete correction and retest
The claim remains limited to the sampled component

adaptation: Use speech, large print, accessible digital text or another safe foundational task with a real standard. Necessary supports are legitimate work conditions. Tasks involving clinical care, driving, weapons, hazardous tools or licensed work require appropriate supervision and are not default practice material.
review: Which basic was reliable across all three attempts, and what repeated error matters more than the most polished single result?

examples.supportive: All three notices preserved the required facts and reading order, while an unstable contact label was corrected and retested.
examples.mixed: One notice looked excellent, but two contained copied dates; the participant targeted fact checking rather than claiming competence.
examples.contradictory: A small safe exercise was used to claim professional qualification or to justify unsupervised hazardous work.
examples.inconclusive: One attractive output was produced without a fixed standard or repeated attempts.

instructional_content.title: Produce and check three dependable event notices

sections.title: Turn a brief into a dependable notice
sections.body: The component is extracting required facts, arranging them for a reader, and checking the result against a fixed specification. Know which source controls each fact, use a tool whose reading order you can inspect, and distinguish accuracy from decoration. A repeatable process is: identify the assigned brief; enter its five facts; preserve the first output; check each fact against that same brief; inspect reading order and access; then correct and retry. The supplied standard is a product specification for this exercise, not a professional credential or an accessibility certification.

sections.title: A reusable layout, with new facts each time
sections.body:
Use a heading for the event name, then labeled lines for date, start–end time, full location and contact. Blank pattern:
EVENT NAME
Date: [day month year]
Time: [start–end]
Location: [venue and address]
Contact: [route]

For an unrelated illustration: Pocket Poetry Hour; 8 August 2027; 14:00–15:00; Maple Reading Room, 3 Orchard Road; poetry@events.example. The facts are fictional. In digital text, keep this order in the underlying text as well as visually; an image-only notice needs an equivalent text version for a text-reading route.

sections.title: The checking standard
sections.body:
F1 — Event name matches the assigned brief.
F2 — Day, month and year match the assigned brief.
F3 — Both start and end times match the assigned brief.
F4 — The full venue and address are preserved.
F5 — The contact route is present and matches the assigned brief.
U1 — A reader can follow the event name, date, time, place and contact in a clear reading order.
U2 — The selected format remains legible and usable with the intended access method; record what was actually inspected.

For each criterion record met, not met, or uninspected, with a short fact or location in the output. Any F1–F5 failure prevents an accuracy pass, regardless of polish. U1 or U2 uninspected means usability remains unverified, not passed. Inspect text order by reading or listening from start to finish. For U2, use the format you actually chose: appropriate zoom or text-reader access for a digital notice, or the selected large-print/speech method. Record that specific condition. A text comparison alone cannot certify every device, reader or print condition. Do not invent a fee, booking rule or access claim that the brief does not supply.

sections.title: Keep the first attempt and its check
sections.body:
Copy this record once for each notice. Keep the notice itself alongside it.

Brief and first-output filename/page:
Tool, format and supports used:
F1 event name: [met / not met / uninspected] — location or discrepancy:
F2 date: [met / not met / uninspected] — location or discrepancy:
F3 start and end times: [met / not met / uninspected] — location or discrepancy:
F4 full venue and address: [met / not met / uninspected] — location or discrepancy:
F5 contact route: [met / not met / uninspected] — location or discrepancy:
U1 reading order: [met / not met / uninspected] — how inspected:
U2 access condition: [met / not met / uninspected] — condition and result:
Reviewer: [self / freely willing reader] — help used:
Correction and separate revised-output filename/page:

Do not turn seven boxes into an average score. One incorrect factual value means
the first output was inaccurate. An uninspected criterion is unknown. Record the
corrected result separately so a successful edit does not erase the original error.

sections.title: Inspect the format you actually used
sections.body:
For digital text, read or listen from the event heading through the contact line.
Check that every fact occurs once in a sensible sequence. Enlarge the text to
200 percent using your usual application controls and inspect every line for clipping
or overlap. If a text-reading route matters for your use, inspect the reading order
with that route too; visually positioned boxes may be read in an unexpected order.
An image-only notice needs a matching text version. Record the application, enlargement
and reading route actually checked; another device or assistive tool remains untested.

For paper, use the intended print size, lighting and reading distance. Read all five
facts without guessing at cramped or faint characters. Enlarge or simplify the notice
if that fails, preserve the earlier version, and inspect the revision. A screen preview
does not establish that the printed copy is usable.

For speech, state the labeled facts in order and allow a replay. Have a freely willing
listener repeat back the date, both times, full place and contact if one is available.
Otherwise record a self-check and leave another listener's usability untested. Necessary
supports are legitimate conditions; these checks are not an accessibility certification.

sections.title: Use an appropriately demanding component
sections.body: The notice route is complete and suitable for practicing a small accuracy-and-presentation task. Keep necessary supports present in all attempts. If this is already routine, choose a safe component from a craft you actually practice, with three comparable input sets and a real recipient or published standard available before beginning. Identify its tools, knowledge, checking method and limits; do not substitute a vague goal such as be professional. This alternate route requires those real materials and their review, so the supplied notice checks cannot certify it. Work requiring licenses or hazardous equipment needs its appropriate established supervision; this route grants no authority.

sections.title: Fresh retest: one changed contact
sections.body: Use the Neighborhood Seed Swap brief again, with exactly one authorized change: replace its contact route with seeds@events.example. Every other fact remains the same. Retain the first version and create a separately labeled revised practice notice.

sections.title: Contact-change retest
sections.body: Apply the single supplied change, preserve the revised output and compare every fact against the updated brief. Explain which correction or pre-publication check made the change reliable. Record an unchanged weakness or error if one remains.

sections.title: Check a plausible but inaccurate notice
sections.body:
Inspect this practice notice against the Neighborhood Seed Swap brief. Use the
same F1–F5 standard before opening the check; do not judge it by its tidy layout.

Neighborhood Seed Swap
Date: 17 May 2027
Time: 10:00–11:30
Location: Willow Community Room, 18 Meadow Lane
Contact: seed-swap@events.example

Which criterion is not met? Name the authoritative fact, the smallest correction,
and the remaining facts you would recheck before calling the revised notice accurate.

sections.title: Target the unreliable basic
sections.body: Compare a 3-by-7 private record: one row per notice, one column per criterion. Identify a repeated error, such as carrying a prior date into the next notice, and a specific process change, such as reading each source fact back after entering it. Retest that feature using the supplied contact change. Keep first attempts and corrected versions separate. Passing these three small samples supports only a bounded observation of this component and the conditions used; broader craft competence and live audience usability remain untested.

checks.title: Check the inaccurate notice
checks.body:
F2 is not met: the source says 16 May 2027, but the notice says 17 May 2027.
Replace 17 with 16 and retain the first output as inaccurate. Then recheck the
event name, start and end times, full venue/address and complete contact against
the same brief. A correct-looking heading or all the other facts cannot cancel
the wrong date. This text comparison checks factual accuracy; U1 and U2 still
need the relevant reading-order and access inspection on the actual output.
criteria: Identify F2 and the mismatch between 16 and 17 May 2027.
Preserve the original and make the date correction in a separate revision.
Recheck F1, F3, F4 and F5 instead of assuming the edit preserved them.
Keep uninspected reading-order or access conditions explicitly unknown.
